{"self_assessment": "Impact: My most important contribution came before building started. I saw that the original plan put the start at the tail, so the tail forks would have had to branch backwards off the body, and the fall can't make that turn. I proposed moving the start to the nose, with one line over the back and one under the belly, both flattening into the tail stem, and the forks opening out gently. Jack redrew the sketch to that design and the table built from it. I also laid the lower tail fork (stroke 4) and kept it standing through the build, restanding dominoes in it several times.

Execution: I inspected the nose area repeatedly. I found that only the first three dominoes fell from the start because the turn right after it was too sharp. I then laid a three-domino bridge from the start row into the top line with a gentler turn, and made small fixes at the start of the top line. I stayed on the tail and the top bridge and left the belly join to Sofia, so we weren't working on the same dominoes.

Collaboration: I split the work clearly, taking the lower fork and asking Omar to take the upper one. I kept pushing for a dry run once the main lines were across. I told people which area I was working on and kept out of the nose when Jack was clearing it. I also kept out of Sofia's belly join.

Leadership: I raised the design problem openly and early, with a concrete alternative the table could adopt. I kept the table's attention on the fall, what actually connects to the start, rather than on how the picture looked. I can't claim the final run is complete: the nose joins were still being worked on when time was called. Even so, the design change and the nose diagnosis were my clearest contributions to the table's result.", "my_share_percent": 25}
